97: And this property that does not serve as a guarantee binds the property that serves as a, etc. Even though one normally does not take an oath concerning land alone -- as we derive in Shevuot (Shevuot 42b:12) -- where the claim included vessels and land, and one is required to take an oath concerning the movable objects, the movable objects bind the land so that an oath must also be taken regarding [the land]. This [verb] "binds" refers to the property that does not serve as a guarantee, and does not [refer] to the court [as a subject of the verb].
